original_question: Determine which finite sets can occur as the set of factorization lengths L(s) of some element s in some numerical semigroup.
target_in_paper: Section 7, the final unnumbered open problem about realizability of sets of lengths of elements in numerical semigroups. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft has the correct target invariant, namely the set of factorization lengths of a single element, and it asks exactly the right realizability question: whether a prescribed set can occur as L(s) for some element s in some numerical semigroup. This matches the paper’s closing open problem in Section 7. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
missing_details: The ambient object should be stated explicitly: a numerical semigroup is an additive submonoid S of N_0, where N_0 denotes the nonnegative integers, containing 0 and with finite complement in N_0. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

The definition of factorization should be included. If S=⟨n_1,...,n_p⟩ is the minimal generating set of S and s∈S, then Z_S(s)={a=(a_1,...,a_p)∈N_0^p : a_1n_1+...+a_pn_p=s}. Section 7 introduces factorizations via this fiber of the factorization homomorphism. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

The length function should be made explicit: for a=(a_1,...,a_p)∈Z_S(s), its length is |a|=a_1+...+a_p, and L_S(s)={|a| : a∈Z_S(s)}. Without this, L(s) is not stand-alone. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

The target family should be phrased as finite nonempty subsets of the positive integers, since a set of lengths of a single element is a set of positive integer values arising from its factorizations. This nonemptiness is an inference from the definitions in Section 7. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

It should be clear that L_S(s) is a set, not a multiset counting how many factorizations have each length. Section 7 distinguishes the set of lengths from other nearby invariants. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

To stay paper-faithful, the question should not broaden to delta sets, elasticity, catenary degree, tame degree, or omega-primality, even though those are defined in the same section. The paper’s final problem is specifically about prescribed sets of lengths. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
refined_question: Characterize the finite nonempty subsets F of the positive integers for which there exist a numerical semigroup S⊆N_0, with minimal generating set S=⟨n_1,...,n_p⟩, and an element s∈S such that, if Z_S(s)={a=(a_1,...,a_p)∈N_0^p : a_1n_1+...+a_pn_p=s} is the set of factorizations of s and L_S(s)={a_1+...+a_p : a∈Z_S(s)} is its set of lengths, then L_S(s)=F. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
justification: The draft is aiming at the last open problem in Section 7. The paper first fixes the ambient notion of numerical semigroup and recalls that such a semigroup has a unique minimal generating set, then in Section 7 defines factorizations, their lengths, and the associated set of lengths L(s). Only after that setup does it ask the realizability question for a prescribed set of lengths. The refined version above makes all of that notation explicit and keeps the scope exactly on the paper’s intended problem, without drifting to the other factorization invariants discussed nearby. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
